title: Cocktail Emoji 🍸 Meaning: Martinis, Happy Hour and Nights Out
description: The cocktail emoji 🍸 is a martini glass with an olive. It means happy hour, bars and dressing up for a night out. See how it differs from 🍹 and 🍷, with examples.
summary: 🍸 shows a stemmed, V-shaped martini glass, usually with an olive. It means a cocktail, happy hour, a bar or lounge, and a polished night out. Compared with beer or tropical drinks it suggests something a little more grown-up and stylish. It has no hidden slang meaning beyond alcohol and nightlife.
meaning: The martini glass is the internet's shorthand for mixed drinks. Whatever is actually in the glass, from a margarita to an espresso martini, 🍸 labels it as a cocktail. People send it to propose drinks after work, to announce they have arrived at a bar, or to say that a rough day calls for something stronger than tea. It is social by default: most 🍸 messages are invitations.

The shape brings associations of its own. The V-shaped glass recalls classic bars, black-and-white films and James Bond ordering his martini shaken, not stirred. That gives 🍸 a more polished image than 🍺 or 🍹. It fits rooftop bars, birthday dinners, bachelorette weekends and anything involving heels or a blazer. Bartenders and cocktail bars use it as their logo-in-miniature, and home mixologists tag recipe videos with it.

It also works as a mood. A single 🍸 after a complaint about work signals the sender is unwinding. Several in a row can describe a lively night, and paired with dizzy or woozy faces it describes being tipsy. Event invitations use it for cocktail attire or a cocktail hour before a wedding dinner. For people who do not drink, mocktail menus have adopted the same glass.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is an invitation or a status update. “🍸 at 7?” sets a plan, “🍸🍸” after a hard week means the sender is ready to go out, and a photo of a bar menu with the emoji says the night has started. It is often used among friends celebrating something, like a new job or a birthday.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Happy-hour announcements and holiday party invites frequently carry 🍸. In professional settings it is fine when the event itself involves drinks, but sending it to a colleague one-on-one can feel like pressure to drink or like a social invitation the other person did not ask for. Teams with non-drinkers sometimes pair it with a note about mocktails.

contexts.label: In captions and bar marketing
contexts.body: Cocktail bars, lounges and restaurants use 🍸 on menus, event posts and happy-hour promotions. Instagram captions put it on rooftop photos, dressed-up selfies and recipe reels. Wedding invitations and programs mark the cocktail hour with it. Alcohol brands also use it, which is why the emoji often appears beside age notices on promotional posts.

A martini, specifically, often a dirty martini.

confusedWith.difference: 🍹 is a fruity drink with an umbrella or garnish, suggesting the beach, vacation and sweet cocktails. 🍸 suggests a city bar and a stronger, more classic drink.
🍷 is a glass of red wine with a rounded bowl. It reads as dinner, relaxing at home or a calm evening, while 🍸 points to a bar and a livelier night.
🥂 shows two champagne flutes touching for a toast. It means congratulations and shared celebration, whereas 🍸 is a single drink and does not imply a toast.

avoid: Avoid sending it to someone who is sober or in recovery unless they have told you they are comfortable with drink invitations.
Do not use it in messages to minors or in school and youth settings.
Keep it out of formal work messages unless the subject is an actual event that serves drinks.
design: A classic martini or cocktail glass: a wide V-shaped bowl on a thin stem and flat base, filled with a clear or pale drink and garnished with an olive on a pick. Some versions tint the liquid or swap the olive for a different garnish, but the silhouette is the same across platforms and instantly recognizable as a cocktail glass.

faqs.q: What does 🍸 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: Usually an invitation to get drinks, which can be friendly or a date proposal depending on context. Sent late at night with no plan attached, it may simply mean the person is out and having a good time.

No. The glass is a martini glass, but people use it for any cocktail: margaritas, cosmopolitans, negronis, espresso martinis and mocktails. For tropical or fruity drinks, 🍹 is the more specific choice.
🍸 is a classic cocktail in a stemmed glass and suggests bars, nightlife and a dressed-up evening. 🍹 is a fruity tropical drink with a garnish, used for beaches, vacations and pool days.

faqs.q: Can I use the cocktail emoji for a non-alcoholic drink?
faqs.a: Yes. Many bars and people use 🍸 for mocktails and zero-proof drinks, since there is no separate emoji for them. Adding a word like mocktail avoids any confusion.
